prompt_c2:
You are a streetscape inventory annotator. Look ONLY at the uploaded streetscape image.
Return JSON ONLY. No markdown, no commentary, no reasoning.
 Task: record what is visible in the scene. Do not score, do not give design advice.
 Schema:
{
"road_type": "highway|arterial|neighborhood_street|alley|plaza|unclear",
"elements": {
"sidewalk": "true|false|unclear",
"bike_lane": "true|false|unclear",
"seating": "true|false|unclear",
"shade_trees": "none|few|many|unclear",
"curb_ramp": "true|false|unclear",
"tactile_paving": "true|false|unclear",
"pedestrian_crossing": "true|false|unclear",
"street_lighting": "true|false|unclear",
"greenery": "none|low|medium|high|unclear",
"vehicle_traffic": "none|light|heavy|unclear",
"bus_stop": "true|false|unclear"
},
"issues": ["no_seating", "little_shade", "no_bike_lane", "poor_accessibility", "narrow_sidewalk", "no_crossing", "high_traffic_exposure"],
"brief": "One or two English sentences describing the visible street scene."
}
 Rules:
- If an element is not clearly visible, use "unclear". Do not guess.
- "issues" may only list problems that are visible. Use [] if none.
- "brief" must mention concrete objects (sidewalk, trees, lanes, benches, ramps, etc.).

Seedlings shall be robust, with straight and full trunks, vigorous branches, evenly distributed and well-developed tissues, and a high degree of lignification. The main trunk of trees shall be clear, with a good structural foundation; street trees shall meet the requirements for nursery release: uniform specifications and regular tree form. Flowering shrubs shall have evenly distributed branches; hedges shall be uniform from top to bottom, with no bare lower portions; spherical seedlings shall have dense branches and leaves. B. The root system shall be well-developed and intact, with many lateral roots and fibrous roots, and no splitting of the roots. C. There shall be a complete and strong terminal bud. Seedlings shall have no mechanical damage, no diseases or pests, no dehydration, and vigorous vitality. D. Trees shall preferably be transplanted seedlings, and field-grown seedlings shall be used with caution. If the tree is a transplanted seedling, all shall be transplanted seedlings of more than one year; if it is a field-grown seedling, root pruning shall be carried out 15–30 days in advance before transplanting. Both transplanted seedlings and field-grown seedlings are required to have full and symmetrical branches and leaves; seedlings with trunks cut back and no canopy are strictly prohibited. E. Seedlings cultivated on nursery sites with conditions similar to the greening land should be used as much as possible, and seedlings propagated from seed are preferred. Cuttings and air-layered seedlings have no obvious or well-developed taproots, and the overall anchoring force of the roots is weak, making them prone to lodging in strong winds. F. A canopy height of 1/3 to 1/2 of the tree height is more appropriate. At the same time, a similar canopy form should be adopted according to the growth characteristics of the corresponding species. The tree form and canopy should not be skewed, and the leaf layer height and density should be moderate. Cup-shaped and umbrella-shaped canopies can reduce frontal strong wind pressure. G. Justice: Analyze whether the environment fairly distributes spatial resources, including Equity (rationality of asset distribution), Fairness (non-discriminatory rules), and Accessibility (barrier-free physical design).
Comfort: Analyze physical perception at a micro-scale, including Thermal Comfort (shade/vegetation), Physical Comfort (paving/seating), and Psychological Comfort (noise/crowding).
Core Indicators: Safety, Livability, Sustainability, Aesthetics, Walkability, and Bikeability.

The analysis must strictly adhere to the persona's characteristics. For example:

Elderly: Focus on resting facilities, slope gradients, and summer shade.
Teenagers: Focus on traffic calming measures and social surveillance (Eyes on the street).

- The IMAGE is the primary evidence. Score only what is visible or reasonably inferable from the photo.
- Section 6 provides retrieved guidelines and research. Use them to interpret the image (what the scene should provide for this persona/indicators), not to invent objects that are not in the photo.
- If retrieved text conflicts with the image, trust the image and say so in the explanation.
- Explanations must cite specific visible objects (benches, ramps, tree shade, lane markings, etc.). When a guideline is used, briefly connect it to those objects.

Seedlings shall be robust, with straight and full trunks, vigorous branches, evenly distributed and well-developed tissues, and a high degree of lignification. The main trunk of trees shall be clear, with a good structural foundation; street trees shall meet the requirements for nursery release: uniform specifications and regular tree form. Flowering shrubs shall have evenly distributed branches; hedges shall be uniform from top to bottom, with no bare lower portions; spherical seedlings shall have dense branches and leaves. B. The root system shall be well-developed and intact, with many lateral roots and fibrous roots, and no splitting of the roots. C. There shall be a complete and strong terminal bud. Seedlings shall have no mechanical damage, no diseases or pests, no dehydration, and vigorous vitality. D. Trees shall preferably be transplanted seedlings, and field-grown seedlings shall be used with caution. If the tree is a transplanted seedling, all shall be transplanted seedlings of more than one year; if it is a field-grown seedling, root pruning shall be carried out 15–30 days in advance before transplanting. Both transplanted seedlings and field-grown seedlings are required to have full and symmetrical branches and leaves; seedlings with trunks cut back and no canopy are strictly prohibited. E. Seedlings cultivated on nursery sites with conditions similar to the greening land should be used as much as possible, and seedlings propagated from seed are preferred. Cuttings and air-layered seedlings have no obvious or well-developed taproots, and the overall anchoring force of the roots is weak, making them prone to lodging in strong winds. F. A canopy height of 1/3 to 1/2 of the tree height is more appropriate. At the same time, a similar canopy form should be adopted according to the growth characteristics of the corresponding species. The tree form and canopy should not be skewed, and the leaf layer height and density should be moderate. Cup-shaped and umbrella-shaped canopies can reduce frontal strong wind pressure. G. Medium-sized seedlings are most suitable. They are more conducive to developing a strong root system, whereas large seedlings have limited root development for a certain period after planting

Purpose of Formulation Under the macro guidance of the “General Provisions,” these Detailed Rules aim at the refined construction of Suzhou’s urban roads, and are expanded and implemented from four directions: human-oriented, quality-oriented, distinctive, and intelligent. They interpret the refined construction of Suzhou’s urban roads in the form of colorful labels, and create urban colorful roads unique to Suzhou. ➢ Human-oriented: Starting from the users of Suzhou’s urban roads, and taking the public’s experience of urban road space as the benchmark, fully consider the comfort, safety, and convenience of public activities, and realize the value shift from “vehicle-centered” to “people-centered.” ➢ Quality-oriented: Vigorously improve the travel quality of people and vehicle traffic in Suzhou, and emphasize the public space function of roads. Appropriately raise the standards for urban road design, construction, and maintenance, extend road service life, and improve users’ comfort of experience. Reflect a road construction level of high appearance and high standards, with attention to detail and control. ➢ Distinctive: Adapt measures to local conditions, and through the embedding of Suzhou-style elements and the creation of road characteristic scenes, highlight Suzhou’s distinctive urban character of integration between tradition and modernity, so that urban roads become an important carrier and display space for the “Jiangnan culture” brand, and continue the city’s historical and cultural lineage. ➢ Intelligent: Deploy intelligent sensing devices along the roadside, together with cloud service platforms, computing and communication facilities, and through data technologies such as autonomous driving and vehicle-road coordination, realize a travel experience of deep interaction among people, vehicles, and road space, assist safe driving and autonomous driving, and create demonstration roads with Suzhou’s smart-city characteristics. 2.
